sentences.text: Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel, Mr. Arun Yadav and Investigating Officer (IO) W/SI Sneh from Police Station Baba Haridas Nagar, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 got married on 11.11.2016 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.
Due to temperamental differences, both the parties started living separately since 03.09.2017.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, the present FIR bearing no. 816/2020 registered at Police Station Haridas Nagar, Delhi for offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/506/323/354/354A/509/34 of IPC against the petitioners.

It is stated that during the pendency of the present case, with the intervention of family and relatives, both the parties had amicably settled all their disputes before the Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 16.11.2022 and had obtained decree of divorce by way of mutual consent from the concerned Court.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, the respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will, volition and without any coercion, pressure or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties before the Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 16.11.2022 and had obtained decree of divorce from the concerned Court.

entities.text: Mediation Centre, Dwarka Courts, New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
8. It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:32:43 items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no.1 and other family members.

9. As per settlement, petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 4,00,000/- to respondent no. 2 in three instalments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 1,25,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of first motion petition under Section 13B (1) of Hindu Marriage Act.
b. Second installment of Rs. 1,25,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion petition under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 1,50,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of present FIR.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final installment of Rs. 1,50,000/- through Demand Draft no. 401922 drawn at Canara Bank dated 12.10.2023 and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

sentences.text: In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the above mentioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 816/2020 registered at Police Station Haridas Nagar, Delhi for offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/506/323/354/354A/509/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. In view of above, the present petition stands disposed of.
